steps.description: Given Zwift's recorded presents beside a terminal that presents through its child and an agent through Direct3D 9, replayed into snapshots second by second, when Zwift is maximized in front, then a terminal on another monitor takes the focus, then the desktop, then FPS and frame time read Zwift's through all of it from its third second on, and a terminal alone that does not fill its monitor never shows FPS.

Given snapshots whose frame slots have no values, as from a service that could not start its session, and snapshots with no slots, as from a service of an earlier version, when the default overlay and the window's items are laid out with a game in front, then the overlay shows no FPS item and the window shows FPS as missing.

Given FPS and frame time items with no lines, and with lines added in the chart, when their values cross each line, then with no lines they stay normal; with lines, FPS warns at or under its warning line and is critical at or under its critical, frame time warns and is critical at or over its lines, and an FPS item whose critical is above its warning is refused.

Given the window with a game's snapshot, when the person adds FPS from the Game device, adds its warning and critical lines and drags the critical, then the item shows in the overlay's list with its value and no lines, the critical line comes under the warning, and cannot pass above it.

Given the service's frame source fed with presents of named processes, when it records with --frames and serves a client, then the recording and every line on the pipe hold process ids and numbers, and no process's name.

Given the installed build, when a person rides Zwift windowed, borderless and in full screen, and free demos present through Direct3D 9, 11 and 12 and Vulkan, then the window's FPS is within 2 % of Zwift's own counter and of PresentMon's beside each demo over a minute, and it keeps showing Zwift while a terminal maximized on the other monitor has the focus and streams text.

Given the installed build with a game presenting at 144 FPS in front, when scripts/measure.ps1 runs for 60 s, then the service stays under 3 % of one core and 80 MB, and with no client connected no thermi-frames session exists.

Given a desktop recorded as administrator, with its board's inputs named as the library names them, each core's VID and both GPUs' voltages, when the catalog is built and searched, then every voltage is listed under its device, found by "volts", by the voltage kind and by its own name, and shown in volts with three decimals under 10 V and two from there; one added as an item has no lines and takes no offset, a sum of two is refused, a CPU's voltage of exactly 0 is missing, and no default overlay reads one. Given the same desktop recorded without admin rights, then each core's VID is the driver's to read and the GPUs' voltages have their values.

Given the app in front presenting 5 frames a second for 6 s, as a window that redraws now and then, and then a game presenting 60, when each second's snapshot is laid out, then the first shows no FPS at all, and the game shows none for its first 2 seconds and 60 from its third.

Given apps that present behind and in front, filling their monitor or not, faster or slower than the game, when each second picks the game, then with no game yet a game behind that fills its monitor is the game at once, never a video in a window; a terminal in front, maximized on the other monitor, never takes over from a game that presents and shows on its own, at 35 FPS nor at its monitor's 180, and is the game at once when the game is minimized; a second game that fills the game's monitor takes over at its third second and keeps it while the first is in front; once it stops, the first is the game again at once; and as seen live, with Zwift maximized at 98 on a monitor at negative X, thermi starting with Chrome full screen on the other at 60 or Wave maximized in front at 180, both presenting from a child, Zwift is the game from the first second, and stays it once Chrome plays a video at 24 in half that monitor beside Wave in the other half.

Given Zwift's recorded presents while OBS captured it, which the kernel tells only as copies of its frames into its window, replayed into snapshots second by second, when Zwift is maximized in front, then FPS reads Zwift's frames from its third second, as many as the recording holds in each second.

Given Zwift's recorded presents riding, in its menus, where the kernel tells them only by BlitRect, and riding again, replayed second by second, when each second is tallied, then every second from the third reads at least 60 FPS and a frame time under 100 ms, never 0.
